1328.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

With manual checkpoint confirmation turned **off**, an evolve design can end on a checkpoint without ever starting the search, and nothing in the UI says so. The session simply sits idle until the user types a reply.

Observed twice, in two shapes:

**A. Auto mode ends on checkpoint 2/4 and the run is never created** (session `665b8e96`, 2026-11-23, `a8573558`)
- New session → `/evolve-design --algorithm puct <task>` → 新建程序演进实验 → uncheck 检查点需要人工确认 → 开始设计 → 发送.
- Transcript ends with: task → 检查点 1/4 → client auto-continue message (`继续完成余下的检查点，并直接调用 create_evolve_run 启动搜索；在搜索启动前不要停下。`) → 检查点 2/4. That is the whole session (4 messages).
- No run card appears; `GET /api/evolve/runs` has no new run; the composer stays idle. No banner, badge or hint says the search was never started.
- Typing `确认检查点 2/4，继续。` continues the design and starts run `b9a8f3da`.

**B. A checkpoint that does not become a card** (session `252ca40d`, run `df752fc3`, 2026-11-22, `checkpointMode: confirm`)
- `09:51:54.709Z` checkpoint 1 renders as a card with 确认，继续; `09:55:00.530Z` confirmed.
- `09:58:27.790Z` checkpoint 2 arrives as **plain prose** (two (a)/(b) questions, no card, no buttons).
- The session sits idle until `11:03:49.635Z` — **65 minutes** — when the tester typed an answer by hand.

**Expected**: when a design's turn ends and this design has no search yet, the client should either carry the next step forward itself, or state plainly that the search has not started and what to send. The code already has the second half of that intent: `use-auto-continue.ts` renders `已停止自动续跑` (`zh.ts:1799-1800`) when the same step comes back, and its header comment says *"a record with nothing to press otherwise reads as a design that hung"* — but that badge can only be drawn **on a card** (`CheckpointCard.tsx:190-194`), so a turn that ends without a card has nowhere to say it.

**Not deterministic**: the same day, run `e344eb1b` (`252ca40d`, `checkpointMode: auto`) went from the user message at `06:25:05.088Z` to the run being created at `06:26:46.085Z` with no manual confirmation in between. So the trigger condition is still unknown; both endings do occur on the same build.

Code pointers:
- `apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-auto-continue.ts` — one push per step, `refusedStep` only surfaces through the card; explicit gates on `run.status === "completed"` and `trailingAutoStep(answer)`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/CheckpointCard.tsx:175-194` — badge lives inside the card.
- `apps/desktop/src/Markdown.tsx:45` — checkpoint blocks are recognised by a fenced `evolve-checkpoint` block; anything else is ordinary prose.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop app (Electron shell around the web UI), Chinese locale `zh-CN`, window 1500×950.
- Commit: `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22), API `4410` / runner `4411` / evolve sidecar `17676`.
- Evolve runtime state: `GET /api/evolve/status` → `{"state":"ready","canInitialize":false,"sandbox":"bwrap"}`.
- Model: Ark DeepSeek (`hasApiToken=true`), permission mode 完全访问.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, Chromium 1228 driven by Playwright 1.61.1.

### Additional Information

- Evidence (desktop screenshots): `~/sd-test/evidence/s205/M1-opened.png` (the stalled session as the user sees it), `C3-checkpoint.png` (a normal manual checkpoint card), `N1-session-stopped.png` (run card after the manual continue).
- Runs involved: `84dcbd84` (puct, manual, succeeded), `17f87374` (openevolve, auto, succeeded — counter-example that auto can work), `b9a8f3da` (puct, auto, stopped by the tester), `e344eb1b` (puct, auto, succeeded — counter-example).
- The same stall shape is reproducible on the web build of the same commit; nothing in the transcript says 「搜索还没开始」.

### Version Information

- `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main branch, 2026-11-22T15:52:52Z).
- Also present in `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21) per the `df752fc3` observation.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop task panel for an evolve run has no **全屏 (Full screen)** and no **查看完整目标 (View full goal)** control, although the capability text for both exists in the desktop string table. A long goal can therefore only be read truncated in the run card.

Steps:
1. Start an evolve run (any algorithm), wait for the run card, click the card.
2. The right-hand panel switches to 任务 and shows the overview, the score chart, the tree and the node list.
3. Its controls are only: 停止 (`button.evolve-task-stop`), 收起面板, and the panel splitter (`调整面板宽度`).

- No 全屏 / 退出全屏 anywhere in the panel.
- No 查看完整目标; the goal is only shown as a one-line truncated title (`写一对标准库 Python 函数 pack(text: str) -> bytes 与 unpack(blob…`), so the constraints of the task cannot be read back while the run is going.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

While a turn is running the permission pill is disabled, so its mode cannot be changed. An evolve design started in 请求批准 (`ask_for_dangerous`) mode therefore stops at its first shell command, and the UI gives no sign that it is waiting for an approval — it keeps showing 正在规划下一步. In my run the design sat like that for **3 hours 31 minutes** until I cancelled the turn.

Steps:
1. New session in the desktop app; leave the permission pill at 请求批准.
2. Type `/evolve-design --algorithm openevolve <task>` and send.
3. The design writes an evaluator, then asks for `Run a shell script in the Session workspace`.
4. Try to switch to 完全访问 while it waits: the pill is `disabled`, `title="这一轮跑完才能切换权限"`.

Observed:
- `GET /api/permission-requests?status=pending` shows the request (`createdAt 2026-11-23T02:11:52.696Z`, summary `Run a shell script in the Session workspace`), still `pending` after 3.5 h.
- The composer shows only 正在规划下一步 and the disabled pill; nothing points at the pending approval, and there is no link or badge to open it.
- Cancelling the turn (`POST /api/sessions/<id>/run/cancel` → 202) then loses the half-written design; the only way forward is to start over with 完全访问.

Expected, any of:
- allow switching the permission mode for subsequent tool calls of the running turn (or offer "allow and switch to 完全访问" on the approval itself), or
- at minimum surface the pending approval prominently (badge/HUD with a link) instead of a passive 正在规划下一步, and keep the request reachable after the turn is cancelled.

Code pointers:
- `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:1113` — `title={running ? TEXT.composer.permissionLocked : TEXT.composer.permissionMode}` and the same `running` flag disables the button.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:259` — `permissionLocked: "这一轮跑完才能切换权限"`.

Note: the same lock makes the *documented* evolve workflow fragile, because evolve needs shell runs and the documented setup is to switch to 完全访问 **before** starting the design; if the user forgets, the only feedback is a silent stall.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop app (Electron shell around the web UI), Chinese locale `zh-CN`, 1500×950.
- Commit: `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22), API `4410` / runner `4411` / evolve sidecar `17676`.
- Session: `fb32e61f-59e3-46d9-a325-2083b3ed3bc2` (the stalled design), pending request id `27b4ceee-b80f-4bd1-9734-f779b24094b3`.
- Evolve runtime `{"state":"ready","canInitialize":false,"sandbox":"bwrap"}`; model Ark DeepSeek.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, Chromium 1228 + Playwright 1.61.1.

### Additional Information

- Evidence: `~/sd-test/evidence/s205/H1-dialog-auto.png` (the dialog before sending), `J1-dialog.png` (the same dialog after switching to 完全访问 — this path works), plus the pending-request JSON quoted above.
- Workaround used: approve via `POST /api/permission-requests/<id>/decision {"decision":"allow_matching"}` — that resolves it, but the UI never offered it.
- The same applies to any long tool-using turn, not only evolve: the turn cannot be re-scoped mid-flight, so the user must cancel and restart.

### Version Information

- `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main branch, 2026-11-22T15:52:52Z).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In a report, an `[evidenceN]` chip opens the 科学记忆 card. When the cited Evidence node was created in a *different Session of the same project*, the card always says **"This memory was not found"**, although the node exists in the memory graph and can be read by an unscoped query. Only citations whose node lives in the report's own Session can be opened.

This is the normal case for project memory: a later Session writes a report that cites literature gathered earlier in the project.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In the desktop client, in Session A (`789fd699-f16a-4248-a59c-4fd6e8fa10d7`), retrieve literature so that Evidence nodes are recorded — e.g. PMID 42888260, 43044265, 40242216.
2. In Session B (`94d52ab1-1718-416f-9675-85d2117e7bb0`), same project, let the agent produce `report.md` that cites those nodes. The report version persists the alias → node map:

```json
[{"id":"4c6f51fa-0c87-46ca-b7aa-cd73f2844207","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence1"},
 {"id":"73392b92-10e9-4963-99d3-9068de05cd64","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence2"},
 {"id":"978921ef-ac48-4bd2-90c8-fb74d7537da9","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence3"}]
```

3. Open that report and press `[evidence1]` (or `[evidence3]`).

**Actual**

```text
证据
科学记忆
没有找到这条记忆
记忆里没有这条记录。它可能已被删除，或记忆服务当前不可用。
```

**Expected.** The card shows the evidence content and its 溯源 (provenance) chain, exactly as it does for evidence created inside the report's own Session.

**Proof that the node exists.** The card's lookup is the node-type query, scoped to the report's Session:

```text
POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type
{"node_types":["Evidence"],"session_id":"94d52ab1-1718-416f-9675-85d2117e7bb0"}
-> {"hits":[],"total":0,"truncated":false}

POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type
{"node_types":["Evidence"]}
-> {"hits":[{"id":"978921ef-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...},
            {"id":"73392b92-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...},
            {"id":"4c6f51fa-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...}], "total":5}
```

Same ids, same graph; only the Session scope differs.

**Root cause**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx:161`:

  ```ts
  const targetSession = reference.sessionId ?? sessionId;
  ```

  The dialog then calls `listMemoryNodes(client, [label], targetSession)` and matches the reference by node id (`matchReferenceHit`, `apps/desktop/src/app/memory.ts:159`). No match → `missing` → "This memory was not found".
- The persisted reference carries **no** `sessionId`. The alias → node map is built by `toChipMap()` in `packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts`, which copies only `id`, `kind`, `label` (and `version` for artifacts) out of the sidecar's `chip_map`. `ComposerReference.sessionId` exists in the schema (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:168`) and the card already honours it — nothing ever writes it.
- So the lookup is scoped to the Session that wrote the report, where a node created elsewhere does not exist.

**Impact if not fixed**

- Every citation that points at project memory from another Session is unreadable in the desktop client: the reader sees "not found" for a record that is there. The citation trail — the whole point of 科学记忆 — is broken exactly in the workflow it exists for (gather once, cite in later Sessions).
- The message says "*It may have been deleted*", which actively implies data loss. An unavailable service already has its own message (`unreachableTitle`/`unreachableBody`, selected in `MemoryCardDialog.tsx:183-190` via `graphTemporarilyUnavailable`), so the "unavailable" half of that sentence never applies — a genuinely missing record and a record outside the Session look identical to the user, and both look like deletion.
- It also corrupts downstream judgement: in the same run a Reviewer specialist reported two numeric claims as unsupported because it saw no `[evidenceN]` mapping, while the mapping existed — it simply cannot be opened.

**Suggested fix**

A. Card-side fallback (smallest, fixes existing reports): when the scoped lookup returns no match and the reference has no `sessionId`, retry once with `session_id` omitted — node ids are globally unique — and use that hit, including its `sessionId` for the provenance chain. A budget refusal (`memory_graph_query_limit`) or an unreachable sidecar must keep rendering as "unavailable", not as "missing".

B. Persist the owning Session: add `session_id` to the sidecar's `chip_map`, copy it in `toChipMap()`, and the card's existing `reference.sessionId` path works with no further UI change. More correct long-term, but references already stored need a backfill, so A is still worth having.

C. Fix the copy in the same change: `memory.notFoundBody` should not claim the record may have been deleted or that the service may be unavailable; say that the record is not in this Session's memory (or drop the sentence in favour of the honest "not found"), and keep the unavailable case on its own message.

A + C is enough to make every already-stored report readable; B can follow as data work.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (Electron shell driving the desktop web UI), viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5), Chromium 1228 driven by Playwright 1.x from the repo's `.e2e` install.
- API `127.0.0.1:4410`, memory-graph sidecar on `127.0.0.1:17675` (`/api/health` reports `memoryGraph: healthy`), runner `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- The failure is independent of the model backend; it reproduces with the same data by re-opening the report.

### Additional Information

- The card distinguishes "no match" (`missing`) from "cannot answer" (`memory_graph_unreachable`, `memory_graph_query_limit`) correctly at the code level; the defect is the scope used for the scoped query, plus the copy that merges both cases.
- Reproducible on reload with no new turn: press the chip again and the same message appears; the report body itself renders all six chips (`artifact1..4`, `evidence1`, `evidence3`).
- Separately observed, not part of this bug: the desktop client has no entry point to delete a single memory record (the API exposes `cleanup/session` and `cleanup/project` only), so a wrong or stale node cannot be removed from the UI.
- Screenshots of the report and of the failing card are in the comment below.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22).
- Reproduced 2026-11-23; the affected report version and the persisted `references` above were read from the store on that build.

1340.body:
Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993 (Nightly #105, attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`, profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`)

Head SHA: `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222`

## Summary

Two independent external causes made this nightly red. Neither is a product defect, but one of them is recorded wrongly, and the recovery path the run needs does not exist in the failed-jobs rerun.

| Job | Result | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11)` | failure | external: model gateway answered 502 / `read ECONNRESET` on both attempts |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Account for real cases` | failure | downstream accounting: `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED` |
| `Gate / merge-gate` | failure | downstream: `CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned` |
| `Report the outcome` | failure | downstream: `RESULT: abandoned` |
| `Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)` | cancelled | external: no macOS runner was ever assigned; no step ran |

Everything else passed on this SHA: L1, UT, ST, Docker, both binary releases, the Windows installer, Coverage, all five mocked workers (`Planned 189; executed 189; passed 189`) and 13 of the 14 real workers, so `Account for real cases` counted `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21`.

## 1. research-11: a provider outage is scored as the product's failure

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825635928, step `Run the frozen real E2E shard`.

The frozen shard held one identity, `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts › Idea Tree real research › real Idea Tree research completes and its result survives a reload` (plan digest `cc111227c7d7`). First attempt:

```
18:22:32.4688386Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:22:34.0581408Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (2.9m)
```

The harness retried the case once in the same job (`18:22:36.7162821Z Repeating 1 failed case(s): …`) and got the identical gateway answer:

```
18:28:46.9978838Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:28:48.8493928Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (5.8m)
```

The shard summary then recorded no provider fault at all:

```
| e2e-real | `cc111227c7d7` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |   (planned/executed/passed/passed-after-retry/failed/provider faults/skipped)
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…/Idea%20Tree%20real%20research/…@linux/amd64/jiuwenswarm
```

That is the gateway's own 502 body, not a product verdict, but the harness files it as `FAIL` with `provider faults 0`, and `Account for real cases` repeats it that way (`- FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…`). The classifier only recognises a gateway fault when the text carries the gateway's own vocabulary (`181001`, `model call failed`, `openai api`, `chat/completions`) — see `GATEWAY_CONTEXT` in `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`. Idea Tree's transport raises its own wording instead, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:250`:

```python
raise RuntimeError(f"Model HTTP {error.code}: {detail}") from error
```

which matches no gateway context, so the fault is dropped. Reproduced at this SHA against the exact recorded message:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e '
import { detectProviderFaultFromErrors } from "./test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs";
const msg = `research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}

expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

Expected: "completed"
Received: "interrupted"`;
console.log("observed  =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg])));
console.log("181001    =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg.replace("Model HTTP 502", "[181001] model call failed, Model HTTP 502")])));
'
observed  => null
181001    => {"code":"provider-transport","status":null}
```

So the same text is a `provider-transport` fault once the gateway's `181001 model call failed` wording is present, and the product's failure when Idea Tree is the one reporting it. `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` pins only the gateway vocabulary (`GATEWAY_500`, `GATEWAY_503`), so nothing covers this second reporter.

That matters beyond cosmetics: the failure is attributed to the product in the run summary and in this report's own accounting, while #1238 (the same class of outage, reported by the gateway itself) was classified `external` / `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The product did retry — `research.py` retries 429/5xx up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` with ≤4 s backoff before raising — and the shard retried the whole case once, so the fault was seen three times over ~10 minutes.

Transient or not: the gateway was healthy again immediately afterwards on the same endpoint. `Real E2E (research-12)` ran 18:29:28–18:32:55 and `Real E2E (research-13)` ran 18:33:27–19:04:23, and both passed, so this is not a configuration or product problem for this SHA.

## 2. macOS desktop installer (arm64): the runner was never assigned

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825643357 (`needs: [policy, l1]`, both succeeded at 16:06:41Z), label `macos-15`.

```
$ gh api /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/jobs/137825643357
{"completed_at":"2026-11-23T16:21:43Z","conclusion":"cancelled","created_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z",
 "labels":["macos-15"],"name":"Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)","runner_id":0,"runner_name":"",
 "started_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z","status":"completed","steps":[]}
```

No step ever started, no runner was assigned (`runner_id: 0`), and nothing in the repository can explain it: the same job on the previous run's runner was healthy (`45073284028`, `macos-15`, 18 steps, success 21:40–22:02Z), the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 120` does not apply while queued, and GitHub recorded no incident on 2026-11-23 (`https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents.json` has no entry that day). The `needs` context inside `merge-gate` reports the job as `abandoned`, and `tier-policy.mjs gate` correctly refuses to treat that as a pass.

The recovery gap is that a cancelled job is not a failed job. `merge-gate` raised:

```
Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned
```

and the only offered bulk operation, `POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun-failed-jobs`, is documented as "re-run all of the failed jobs and their dependent jobs" — nothing in it recreates a job that never started, so `macos-desktop` would still be `abandoned` in the rerun's `needs` and the gate would fail again with the same message. The specific-job endpoint (`POST /actions/jobs/137825643357/rerun`) is the only thing that can re-run that job, and even that alone cannot pass the gate while `real-scheduled` is still a failure from attempt 1 — recovering this run needs both, or a fresh run.

## 3. Downstream jobs fail as designed

- `Account for real cases` (job 137939547826): `### Real E2E: FAIL`, `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0`, `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`. It runs no model call; it reconciled 14 shard artifacts, including `real-e2e-results-research-11`, and the missing pass is real evidence, not an accounting bug.
- `merge-gate` (job 137939753365): declared `"real-scheduled": {"result": "failure"}` and `"macos-desktop": {"result": "abandoned"}` itself, so the gate message names its own inputs.
- `Report the outcome` (job 137939983308): `RESULT: abandoned` fails the `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` step. Expected: "a skipped or cancelled gate is not a pass either".

## What was checked / how a rerun behaves here

- All five job records of this run through `/actions/runs/45212568993/jobs` and each failed job's own log; the `needs` JSON printed by `merge-gate`; the accounting output of `Account for real cases`.
- Whether a failed-jobs rerun re-uses attempt-1 artifacts: it does. In run 45073284028 attempt 2 the identical four jobs were re-run after `Real E2E (research-8)` failed and the run went green, consuming the other shards' attempt-1 artifacts, and re-uploading the same artifact names (`real-e2e-results`, `e2e-results`, `real-e2e-verdict`, `case-execution-details.md`) produced a second artifact per name rather than a conflict.
- Why no failed-jobs rerun was made here: every failed job is downstream of one of the two external causes above, but the resulting rerun cannot turn the run green, for the reason in section 2. A rerun would spend another paid research-11 shard to reproduce a red `macos-desktop` gate. A full re-run (`POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun`) or a fresh `Nightly` dispatch re-runs ~14 real workers and ~2 h of gate time, and is a scheduling decision for the repository, not a repair.

## Related work

- #1238 — same class of gateway fault (stream reset mid-answer), but reported by the gateway, so it was classified `external`/`PROVIDER_FAULT`. That is the attribution this run did not get.
- #1239 — an earlier research-11 nightly report; different root cause (managed Python base setup `failed`, case `BLOCKED`, nothing executed). This run executed the case and lost it at the gateway.
- #1327 — Idea Tree ends the whole research as `interrupted` on one unusable model answer. This run's `interrupted` came from a transport 502, not from answer validation, so it is a different entry into the same terminal state.
- #1339 (open) — isolate tagged case retries. It does not change this outcome: the retry ran, and the provider was still returning 502.
- #813 — the earlier L3 version of "one gateway outage fails the gate"; the accounting and retry handling in this run are the later form of that work.

## What would close this

1. Let the provider-fault classifier recognise Idea Tree's own reporter, e.g. a `Model HTTP <5xx>:` raised by `research.py`'s transport beside the body that follows it, so this outage is reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT` (status 502) instead of `FAIL`, and add a regression case for the exact text above to `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.
2. Decide the recovery route for a distribution job that was never started: the gate must keep failing on it, but "re-run failed jobs" cannot fix it, so the documented remedy has to be a specific-job re-run or a fresh run. A person with Actions write decides which.

Environment: `ubuntu-26.04` hosted runners for the Linux jobs, `macos-15` for the desktop job, Windows runner for the installer; CI Node 22.19.0; profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`, model `deepseek-flash` through the CI gateway; version stamp `nightly-20261124-9da58ad`.

### Checklist

- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The L1 step `Enforce changed-path test evidence` compares a pull request with the **base recorded in the event payload** while the checked-out tree is the **merge commit**. When `main` moves after the pull request is opened, every commit `main` gained in between is attributed to the pull request. On #1297 that produced seven blocking `added source has no test mapping` lines for files the pull request never touched, and `merge-gate` failed only because L1 failed.

Observed on PR #1297, head `7024be557e9a3174ebb5dec0e8b81dee7ce53b01` (CI run [45309655627](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45309655627), job `L1 (static checks)` 138162322793):

```
CI_BASE_SHA: 9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8
CI_HEAD_SHA: 4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4
...
Changed-path source-test policy failed:
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/api/reviewer.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/permission-summary.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/reviewer/ReviewCard.tsx
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/reviewer/presentation.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/settings/McpImportMenu.tsx
- added source has no test mapping: apps/web/src/permission-summary.ts
- added source has no test mapping: packages/schema/src/permission-description.ts
```

Why those are not this pull request's files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes `CI_BASE_SHA: github.event.pull_request.base.sha` and `CI_HEAD_SHA: github.sha`. For a `pull_request` run `github.sha` is the merge commit, and `actions/checkout` fetches exactly that (`+4f0eaa07…:refs/remotes/pull/1297/merge` in the same log).
- `4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4` is `Merge 7024be55… into d13cead9…`, with parents `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5` (current `main`) and `7024be55…` (the pull request head).
- `9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8` is this branch's merge base with `main` — the base recorded when the pull request was opened — and the pull request still reports it after `main` moved to `d13cead9`.
- `.ci/changed-path-check.mjs` therefore ran `git diff 9eab9760 4f0eaa07`, which contains every commit `main` gained between `9eab9760` and `d13cead9`.
- All seven blocking paths were added to `main` in that interval; for example `apps/web/src/permission-summary.ts` does not exist at `9eab9760`.
- The pull request changes five files, and the only inventory source among them is `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts`, which the same run reported as `existing changed source has no test mapping` — a warning, not a failure. **The pull request's own diff is clean under this policy.**

Impact: any pull request that is behind `main` fails L1 and, through it, `merge-gate` — on a rule it does not violate, with a message naming files its author never wrote. The workaround is to rebase (that makes the recorded base equal the merge commit's first parent and the check passes), but it is undiscoverable from the failure text and it clears approvals.

This is the same class of defect as #1271 (the release-version gate read the merge tree against the recorded base, so a stale branch looked like a version bump); #1269/#1272 fixed that by comparing the tested merge commit with **its own first parent** and validating the topology.

#### Suggested fix

Use the merge commit's first parent as the comparison base instead of the event's recorded base: require the checked-out head to be a two-parent merge whose second parent is `pull_request.head.sha`, take the first parent as the base, and fail explicitly with a named error when the topology is not that. Note that `git merge-base <recorded base> <merge commit>` returns the stale base itself, so it is not a substitute.

#### Regression case

`.ci/changed-path-check.test.mjs` already builds real temporary histories, so the case belongs there:

1. `main` commit `B`;
2. `main` commit `M` that adds an unmapped behavioral source (e.g. `services/runner/src/New Runner.ts`);
3. pull-request commit `P` on `B` that adds only a test or doc file;
4. merge commit with parents `M` and `P`;
5. run with `CI_BASE_SHA=B`, `CI_HEAD_SHA=<merge>`;
6. expect exit 0 with no blocking entry for `M`'s file (a warning or `0/1 mapped` line is fine).

Today that run reports `M`'s file as an added unmapped source and exits 1, so the case distinguishes the fix from the current behaviour.

| --- | --- |
| Repo state | `main` `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5`; incident on PR #1297 head `7024be557e9a3174ebb5dec0e8b81dee7ce53b01`, merge commit `4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4`, recorded base `9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8` |
| Where | `.ci/changed-path-check.mjs`, invoked by the `Enforce changed-path test evidence` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (L1 job) |
| Introduced by | `d13cead9…` (`test: complete coverage and CI gate hardening`), which added the script, its test file and the sources it now reports |
| CI evidence | L1 job 138162322793 failed on `Enforce changed-path test evidence`; `merge-gate` job 138163564882 failed on `Require all jobs selected by this event` |
| Workaround | rebase onto current `main`; the comparison then starts at `d13cead9` and only the pull request's files are checked |

### Additional Information

- A pull request that is up to date with its base is unaffected: its recorded base equals the merge commit's first parent.
- The warning list of such runs is polluted the same way (`existing changed source has no test mapping` for files `main` touched after the branch was opened), so the output cannot be read as "what this pull request changed".
- The check is correctly load-bearing for the pull request's own additions: the `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts` warning in the same run shows the mapping policy still applies to the diff this pull request really produced.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** The "new evolve experiment" dialog lets the user set custom evolution parameters, but shows no range, unit or interaction rule for any of them. Values outside the server's limits are coerced or rejected later, so the run does something other than what was typed.

**Where it happens**

1. Open a Session, then the Session menu (`会话设置`) → `程序演进实验`.
2. Tick `自定义演进参数` (`Custom evolution parameters`).
3. The panel offers `＋ 添加参数`, `上传 JSON`, `生成起始参数`. Add `expansions` and type `40`.

**Actual.** The dialog accepts the value without a word. The run then starts with `expansions: 37`: the server enforces

- `expansions <= 40`
- `maxTokensPerCall * expansions <= maxTokens` (with the defaults `16000 * 37 <= 600000`)
- `maxSeconds` is not settable at all (fixed at 7200 s)

and none of these rules is visible anywhere in the dialog. The parameter panel's only hint is the generic "为参数设定起始值。勾选的参数会由演进自动尝试不同取值；未勾选的始终使用起始值。"

**Expected.** Each parameter names its range and unit next to the field, and a value that cannot be honoured says so while it is typed ("40 exceeds 40? no — but 16000 × 40 > 600000, so it will run as 37"), instead of being quietly rewritten at run-creation time.

**Impact**

- The number the user typed is not the number that runs, with no record of why; the only way to learn the rules is to read a finished run's record and compare.
- A user tuning a search budget cannot tell whether a poor result came from the task, the budget or a coerced parameter.
- `maxSeconds` looks settable (it is just another key in the same editor) but is ignored, which reads as a broken setting rather than a fixed limit.

**Suggested fix.** Render the constraints with the fields (min/max/step/unit plus the cross-field formula), validate on input, and when a value has to be adjusted show the effective value in the dialog before the run is created.

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI), viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, evolve runtime on `127.0.0.1:17676` (`/api/evolve/status` = `ready`, sandbox `bwrap`), Chromium 1228 via Playwright.
- Model backend: `Ark DeepSeek` (deepseek-v4.1-flash).

### Additional Information

- Reproduced on `a8573558` and again on `9da58ad6`; the dialog markup and copy are unchanged between the two.
- Screenshot of the empty parameter panel (no range, no formula, no unit) is in the comment below.
- Related: the run record is the only place the effective `expansions` value appears, which is why this is easy to miss.

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In the `导出会话` (export Session) dialog, the number shown as `预计大小` (estimated size) is the size of the **uncompressed** archive, while the file that is actually downloaded is gzip-compressed and roughly 4x smaller. The headline number therefore overstates the download by more than a factor of four.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open any Session → Session menu → `导出会话`.
2. Wait for the size to be computed.

**Observed**

- `必要导出` (essential export): `预计大小 812.5 KB`.
- `完整导出` (full export): `预计大小 102.9 MB`.
- The small print under the list says `未压缩估算 812.5 KB`, and `未压缩上限：5.0 GB` — so the estimate is explicitly the unpacked size.

**Actual download.** Pressing `开始导出` downloads `<Session title>.sdresearch`:

```text
189,132 bytes
$ file <Session title>.sdresearch
gzip compressed data, from Unix, original size modulo 2^32 824320
```

824,320 B unpacked ≈ 805 KB matches the 812.5 KB estimate, so the estimate is internally consistent — it is simply not the size of what the user gets.

**Expected.** The number next to `预计大小` is the size of the file that will be downloaded, or the two numbers are shown together (`约 189 KB（未压缩 812 KB）`).

**Impact**

- Anyone deciding whether an export fits somewhere (attachment limit, disk, upload) plans for 4x the space they need. The same gap was seen earlier on a research-package export: estimate `102.9 MB`, downloaded `29,073,956 B`.
- Because the two numbers never match, a user may suspect the export is incomplete rather than compressed.
- On a large Session the gap is the difference between "this is fine" and "this is too big to send".

**Suggested fix.** Estimate the compressed size (or label the headline as the unpacked size and put the download size next to it), and keep the `5.0 GB` limit labelled as what it measures.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Two small feedback gaps on the evolve run card: stopping gives no in-progress state, and clicking the card toggles the detail panel instead of expanding the card, which is not what the card's affordance suggests.

**Part 1 — Stop has no visible intermediate state**

1. Start an evolve run and open its card.
2. Press `停止`.

Observed: the card goes from `正在优化 / 已耗时 N` straight to `已停止` after about **4.6 s** (measured on run `b9a8f3da`, `06:19:15.232Z → 06:19:19.838Z`). There is no `正在停止…` state, no disabled button state and no "cancelling N in-flight candidates" line, so for a few seconds after the click the UI looks like it did nothing. Nodes that were in flight stay in the list with `-` as their score.

Expected: the button flips to a busy state (`正在停止…`) immediately, and the card says what is being wound down.

**Part 2 — Clicking the card is not "expand"**

The card looks like a collapsible summary (title + state + elapsed time) and shows a `›`, but pressing it opens/closes the right-hand detail panel rather than expanding the card in place. The panel is where the actual numbers live (总览 / 曲线 / 优化树 / 预算), so a reader who expects an inline expand sees nothing happen on the card itself and concludes the card is not interactive.

**Impact**

- On a long run, a user who presses `停止` has no way to tell whether the click landed and may press it again (it disappears in the stopped state, so the second press hits nothing).
- The only surface with real progress information is behind a click whose effect is not what the card's shape implies; on a wall-clock-length run this is the difference between trusting the card and ignoring it.

**Suggested fix.** Render `正在停止…` as soon as the stop request is accepted (and keep the button disabled until the state settles), and make the card's affordance honest: either expand inline or label the control as opening the task panel.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Pressing `开始设计` (Start design) in the "new evolve experiment" dialog does not start anything. The dialog closes and the task text is dropped into the composer, but no message is sent and nothing says that a second action is required, so the button's own promise ("start design") is not what happens.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a Session with some history.
2. Session menu → `程序演进实验`.
3. Pick an algorithm, type a task (`写一个把文本无损压缩的函数，分数是压缩比。`), press `开始设计`.

**Observed** (`9da58ad6`)

```text
before:              composer = ""
after 开始设计:       composer = "写一个把文本无损压缩的函数，分数是压缩比。"
dialog still open:   0
message count:       15 → 15   (nothing was sent)
send button:         enabled
```

So the click fills the composer with the task text and leaves the send button for the user to press. Nothing on screen says "check the box below and press send"; the dialog simply disappears.

**Expected.** Either the button sends the request (what its label says), or it is labelled for what it does (`填入输入框`) and the composer is focused with a one-line hint that one more press sends it. In an empty Session, pressing it must not be a silent no-op.

**Root cause (client).** `开始设计` builds the evolve request into the composer and closes the dialog; the send action stays with the user. The dialog's copy doesn't mention that hand-off, so the only feedback after the click is the dialog vanishing.

**Impact**

- A first-time user presses `开始设计`, sees the dialog close and nothing happen, and concludes the feature is broken (or that a run is already going and the UI is stuck).
- Users who do notice the composer may send the plain task text without the `/evolve-design` command, so the request runs as a normal chat turn instead of an evolve design.
- In a Session with no project selected the click appears to do nothing at all.

**Suggested fix.** Send on click (and keep the dialog open on failure), or rename to `填入输入框` and focus the composer with a visible "press send to start" hint.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › 沙箱网络`, pressing `开放网络` (Open network) does nothing: no confirmation dialog, no mode change, no disabled state and no explanation. The mode stays on `无网络` even with a real mouse click.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open `设置` → `沙箱网络` (`Settings › Sandbox network`).
2. Press `开放网络`.

**Observed** (`9da58ad6`, two scripts, one programmatic and one real mouse click at the button's centre)

```text
before: buttons = [无网络(active), 域名白名单, 开放网络, 保存]
after : buttons = [无网络(active), 域名白名单, 开放网络, 保存]
```

Neither path produces the confirmation described in the documentation of this setting ("开放网络意味着沙箱里的任何代码都能访问任意地址，只保留私网过滤。确定要这样吗？"), and the active mode never moves. On `bbdbdd5` (2026-11-22) the same step did open that confirmation and, once confirmed, `开放网络` became active — so this is a regression on the current main.

**Expected.** Pressing `开放网络` opens the confirmation; cancelling leaves the mode unchanged; confirming makes it active. If network mode changes are not allowed in this configuration, the button is disabled and says why.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** The Scientific-memory status does not check the thing the queries need. A memory-graph service that answers its unauthenticated health endpoint but rejects every query with `401` is reported as `运行正常` (`Running normally`), and every citation card then says only `暂时读不到科学记忆`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run a memory-graph sidecar whose internal token differs from the API's `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_INTERNAL_TOKEN` (in a mixed local stack this happens by accident; I hit it on `127.0.0.1:17674`, a sidecar started by someone else).
2. Open `设置 › 科学记忆`.
3. Press a citation chip in any report.

**Observed**

```text
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer wrong' \
    -d '{"node_types":["Evidence"]}' http://127.0.0.1:17675/query/by-node-type
401    ->   {"detail":"invalid internal token"}

Settings page:  运行正常
Citation card:  暂时读不到科学记忆 / 记忆服务没有响应。稍后再试一次。
```

The status surface reports health, the query path reports an authentication failure, and the user is told "the memory service did not answer" — which is false; it answered `401`.

**Expected.** The status row separates "service up but this process cannot authenticate" from "service down", and the citation card's `memory_graph_unreachable` reason distinguishes an auth rejection from a transport failure. `运行正常` must not be shown while every query is refused.

**Impact**

- A misconfigured token looks like a healthy installation; the only symptom is that citations stop opening, with copy that blames a timeout.
- Users retry, restart the sidecar and re-check health — none of which can help, because nothing points at credentials.
- It also hides this class of misconfiguration from support: the status page says there is nothing to fix.

**Suggested fix.** Probe the authenticated path (a cheap `by-node-type` with an empty type list) for the status row, and give the auth rejection its own reason/copy instead of folding it into `memory_graph_unreachable`.

### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client has no way to archive a Session. The API exposes archive/restore routes (`services/api/src/http/index.ts` routes `/archive|restore`), but `apps/desktop/src` contains no reference to archiving at all, so the capability is unreachable from the only client most users run.

Motivation: Sessions accumulate (one per experiment), and the sidebar already folds older ones behind `显示更多` (see #1348). Without archive, the only way to shorten the list is to delete, which also removes the artifacts and the evidence trail — so users keep everything, and the fold gets worse.

### Design Ideas

- Add `归档会话` to the Session menu (`会话菜单`), next to 重命名 / 导出会话 / 删除, with a confirmation line saying what archiving keeps (data and artifacts stay, only the list entry moves).
- Surface archived Sessions in the sidebar behind a `已归档` filter/toggle, not mixed into the normal list.
- Reuse the existing API routes rather than adding new ones; the client only needs a client method plus the menu entry and the filter.
- Alternative considered: keep deletion only and lean on the fold. Rejected — deletion destroys the evidence trail and is not reversible.

### Involved Public APIs

No new public API is expected: the archive/restore routes already exist server-side. If a list filter is added, it should extend the existing Sessions listing query rather than change its shape.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Sidebar list rendering and the `显示更多` fold (#1348).
- Session deletion flow, which today is the only destructive path in that menu.
- Export (#1347) — an archived Session should still be exportable.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- UI test: archive a Session from the menu, assert it disappears from the active list and appears under `已归档`; restore it and assert it returns with its artifacts intact.
- Regression: archiving must not delete data — after archive + restore, the Session's artifacts, versions and citations still open.
- Guest path: a Session that is running cannot be archived (or the run is stopped first) — assert the state, not a silent failure.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `归档会话` exists in the Session menu and archives the Session without deleting its artifacts or evidence.
- [ ] Archived Sessions are reachable through a visible filter/toggle and can be restored.
- [ ] The active list shrinks accordingly, and the fold count (#1348) reflects the archived set.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of today's Session menu (重命名 / 导出会话 / 删除, no archive entry) is in the comment below.
- Found while testing D2-09; that test was removed from the map because the entry point does not exist.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client cannot delete a single Scientific-memory record. The memory settings page offers only the global switch, and the citation card is read-only; the API has `cleanup/session` and `cleanup/project`, but `apps/desktop/src` has no call to either, so a wrong or stale record can only be removed by wiping a whole Session's or project's memory.

Motivation: evidence nodes are extracted automatically, so a bad extraction (wrong paper, a garbage abstract, a duplicated record) ends up cited by later reports and there is no way to remove just that node. Today the only remedy is `cleanup` on the whole scope, which throws away the good records with the bad one.

### Design Ideas

- Add `删除这条记忆` to the citation card (`MemoryCardDialog`) for Evidence nodes, with a confirmation line naming what else is linked to it.
- Alternatively (or additionally) a record list in `设置 › 科学记忆` with per-row delete, since the card is only reachable from a citation.
- Keep `cleanup/session|project` as-is for bulk resets; the new action is the single-record counterpart.
- Alternative considered: leave it API-only and document it. Rejected — most users of the desktop client never call the API.

### Involved Public APIs

A single-record deletion endpoint may be needed (or a narrower parameter on the existing cleanup route). It should be explicit about what happens to artifacts and claims that cite the record — dangling citations must degrade the same way an already-missing node does (see #1334).

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Citation card and the `missing` state (#1334): after a delete, chips that cited the record must render the "not found" path rather than crash.
- Scientific-memory settings page and the sidecar's write path (delete must go through the service, not edit the graph files).

### Test Design and Test Plan

- UI test: delete one Evidence node from its card; assert the card closes, the node disappears from the memory list, and other nodes in the same Session survive.
- Regression: a report citing the deleted record still renders; pressing that chip shows the not-found state (not an error page).
- Bulk path unchanged: `cleanup/session` still removes everything in a Session.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single Scientific-memory record can be deleted from the desktop client, with a confirmation.
- [ ] Deleting one record leaves the rest of the Session's and project's memory intact.
- [ ] Existing citations to the deleted record degrade to the not-found state instead of breaking the card.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

1360.author: zhaozhaozz
1360.body:
### 🚀 Background Description
During peak development hours, concurrent PR and merge-queue runs exhaust the organization's shared GitHub-hosted runner concurrency pool, causing 6–14 minute queuing delays across merge-queue and short gate jobs. The longest Linux jobs in `merge_group` are the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `UT`, which together consume ~60 runner-minutes per merge-queue run while waiting in the same hosted pool.

We have a dedicated 16 vCPU / 60 GiB Linux x86_64 host running 4 isolated Dockerized self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`) with verified bubblewrap user-namespace support, isolated per-container network/PID namespaces, pre-warmed local `/ci-cache` storage, and post-job cleanup hooks.

### Design Ideas
- Keep `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as the single shared workflow definition without duplicating jobs or adding per-runner port-allocation shell blocks (each runner container already isolates its own network namespace).
- Gate self-hosted routing strictly behind **both** `github.event_name == 'merge_group'` (trusted code reviewed and enqueued) and a repository variable toggle `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off, allowing instant fallback to `ubuntu-latest` without a code change).
- Route only the 4 heavy merge-queue Linux jobs to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`:
  - `ut`
  - `e2e` matrix shards `standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, and `research`
- Keep all `pull_request` runs (including forks), short mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `st`, `desktop-mocked`, `real-merge` (L3 with model secrets), `Nightly`, `Release`, and `Package` runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Raise `e2e` matrix `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` so the two hosted short shards and three self-hosted heavy shards start concurrently without waiting behind each other.
- Avoid cross-region `actions/cache@v4` download/upload overhead on self-hosted containers by:
  - Skipping `actions/cache@v4` (and `setup-node` / `setup-uv` remote caching) when a job runs on a self-hosted container.
  - Using a small helper script `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` to lock and reuse a hash-keyed read-only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` tree under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR}/jiuwenswarm` (removing `.git` after first setup so concurrent containers hit `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`'s pre-installed verify-only fast path).
  - Making `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent (`if ! bwrap ...; then sudo apt-get ...; fi`) so pre-provisioned containers skip `sudo apt-get`.
  - Respecting pre-set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache` in `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (consistent with `UV_CACHE_DIR` today) so containers reuse pre-warmed Chromium and Python 3.12 with zero workflow branching.

### Involved Public APIs
None. Internal CI workflow routing, test harness cache environment variable fallbacks, and `.ci/` scripts/tests only.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` and `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy routing and mocked E2E matrix generation)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`policy`, `e2e-plan`, `ut`, `e2e` jobs)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (honoring `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache` when set)
- `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` (local hash-keyed JiuwenSwarm cache helper)
- `.ci/README.md` and `.ci/*.test.mjs` contract tests

### Test Design and Test Plan
- Unit/contract tests verifying:
  - Self-hosted routing is **only** enabled when `event === 'merge_group'` AND `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE === 'true'`; all `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` events always resolve to `ubuntu-latest` even if the variable is set.
  - `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` assigns `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]` + `self_hosted: true` strictly to `standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, and `research` when enabled, while `governed` and `literature` stay `ubuntu-latest` + `self_hosted: false`.
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gates remote `actions/cache`, `setup-node` cache, `setup-uv` cache, and `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` properly, keeps `max-parallel: 5` on `e2e`, and probes `bwrap` before `sudo apt-get`.
  - Hermetic bash tests for `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` covering cache miss + `.git` removal + `.ready` marker, cache hit fast path, and failed install cleanup.
  - Regression test verifying `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` preserves caller-provided `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` / `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` / `npm_config_cache` while keeping existing defaults when unset.
- Commands to run: `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`, `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, and `node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` runs never route `ut` or `e2e` to self-hosted runners, regardless of `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE`.
- [ ] When `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset or not `'true'`, `merge_group` runs keep existing `ubuntu-latest` routing and remote caching unchanged.
- [ ] When `event === 'merge_group'` and `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`, `ut` and the three heavy mocked shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) route to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]` using local `/ci-cache` and skipping remote `actions/cache`, while `governed` and `literature` stay on `ubuntu-latest` with `max-parallel: 5`.
- [ ] `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` in `ut` and `e2e` skips `sudo apt-get` when `bwrap` already passes its probe.
- [ ] `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` honors pre-set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache`, falling back to existing defaults when unset.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:selftest`, `pnpm ci:l1` (and PR CI `merge-gate`).

### Additional Information
Rollout is two-step: merge with `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` unset (no behavioral change), then enable the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true` to cut over merge-queue traffic with instant rollback capability.

### Checklist

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Exporting a Session package that comes out at **189 KB** takes **38.1 s**, and the dialog needs **6.07 s** before it can show the size estimate at all. Everything else in the same client at the same moment answers in milliseconds, so this is not a slow server or a slow network.

**Measured on `9da58ad6`** (single Session, 11 workspace files, one artifact with citations; headless Chromium, localhost, `~/sd-test/data` = 1.8 GB / `versioning` = 1.7 GB)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Session menu → `导出会话` → `预计大小` shown (`正在重算…` in between) | **6.07 s** |
| `开始导出` → file delivered | **38.1 s** |
| Package produced | 189,131 B (`.sdresearch`, gzip; 824,320 B unpacked) |
| For comparison: `GET /api/projects` | 1 ms |
| `GET /api/models` | 0.6 ms |
| `POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type` (scoped) | 15 ms |

Two runs on different days agree: the same Session's estimate took 6.1 s and its export ~38 s; the earlier full export (102.9 MB unpacked / 29 MB downloaded) took minutes.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a Session that has artifacts (this one: `SK 自旋玻璃基态搜索演进`).
2. Session menu → `导出会话`; time until `预计大小` shows a number.
3. Press `开始导出`; time until the file lands.

**Expected.** A 189 KB package should take low single-digit seconds; the estimate should appear quickly (or be computed server-side once per Session and cached).

**Where it likely goes (needs instrumentation to confirm).** The capacity preflight is *not* the cost — `measureResearchPackageCapacity` is `statfs` + `MemAvailable` (`services/api/src/research-package-preflight.ts:72`), i.e. sub-millisecond. Both the estimate route and the export route call it, so the time is in enumerating/writing the package content: the export route (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1549-1561`) starts a task through `packageExports.start(...)` after `sized.archiveBytes` is computed, and the size computation touches the same data. Splitting `measure size` / `gather records` / `read CAS objects` / `write archive` timings would localise it immediately.

**Impact**

- Exporting is the only way to hand a Session to someone else (or to archive it), and it is slow enough that users start it and walk away; a partial failure after 38 s costs the whole wait.
- The dialog freezes its own numbers behind `正在重算…` for 6 s, so even checking "how big is this going to be" is a wait.
- It scales with the store, not with the package: the same operation on a 190 KB package already costs tens of seconds on a 1.8 GB data dir.

**Suggested fix.** Cache the size estimate per Session (invalidated on artifact change) instead of recomputing on every dialog open; stream the package write with a progress indicator; and add per-stage timing logs so a regression is visible.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI at a vite dev server), 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5), 80 cores; API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright with downloads enabled; `~/sd-test/data` 1.8 GB total, `versioning/` 1.7 GB.

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of the dialog with the finished estimate is in the comment below; the delivery timing is from the Playwright `download` event, and the estimate timing from the moment the Session menu was clicked until a number appeared.
- Related: #1347 (the estimate shows the uncompressed size) — same dialog, different defect.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Settings pages block until their own request returns, and two of them make the reader wait about a second: switching to `模型用量` (`Model usage`) took **998 ms**, and the first visit to `运行环境` (`Runtime`) took **1.52 s** before the `正在读取…` placeholder went away. The other 13 pages are fine (280–500 ms), so the cost is per-page data, not the dialog itself.

**Measured on `9da58ad6`** (1500x950, `zh-CN`, click → `.settings-main` rendered; one page after another in one session)

| Page | Time |
|---|---|
| `模型用量` | **998 ms** |
| `联网搜索` / `沙箱网络` / `网络代理` / `导出记录` / `通用` | 298 / 309 / 307 / 288 / 279 ms |
| `技能` / `专家` / `MCP 服务器` / `Idea Tree` | 301 / 300 / 388 / 425 ms |
| `模型` / `科学记忆` / `超时` | 474 / 496 / 468 ms |
| `运行环境` (first visit) | **1,521 ms** (shows `正在读取…`) |
| `运行环境` (revisit, cached) | 288 ms |

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open `设置`.
2. Click `运行环境` first time after load — the page shows `正在读取…` for ~1.5 s before the builtin Runner appears.
3. Click `模型用量` — the page is blank until the usage summary arrives (~1 s).

**Expected.** The page shell renders immediately (title, sections, skeleton rows) and the numbers fill in; the fetch is shared/cached between visits. A settings page should not show an empty body while its data loads, and a revisit should not re-fetch what has not changed.

**Why it happens.** Each settings page fetches its own data on mount and renders nothing (or a single placeholder line) until it resolves; `运行环境` additionally probes the Runner before it can draw the card. Nothing is prefetched, so the first visit pays the full round trip and the dialog body is empty meanwhile.

**Impact**

- Opening settings feels heavy: 15 pages, two of them a second or more, and the blank body gives no hint that something is loading (the `正在读取…` line is easy to miss in a long page).
- Users bounce between pages while a run is going; each revisit repeats the work because there is no cache.
- It is fixable without touching the API: render a skeleton, prefetch the two heavy panels when the settings dialog opens, and keep the last response for the session.

**Suggested fix.** Skeleton/shell first paint; prefetch `模型用量` and `运行环境` on dialog open; cache per-dialog responses (the data is already scoped to `today`/`last 7 days`, so a short TTL is enough).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Importing a `.sdresearch` package that contains an evolution run copies that run into the run list under a **new id**, with every value identical to the original. Importing the same package twice produces three runs that are the same run. Run lists, per-Session statistics and "does this Session have an active run" checks all see the copies as separate runs.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In a Session that has a finished evolution run, `导出会话` → `必要导出`, save the package.
2. `导入会话` → pick the package → `导入`. Note that the imported Session opens as a read-only snapshot.
3. Import the same package once more.
4. Read `GET /api/evolve/runs`.

**Observed** (2026-11-24, `9da58ad6`)

```text
0098af62  succeeded  session 5293e460  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
46ea4b76  succeeded  session fe4d2e3c  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
de2b933f  succeeded  session b163af95  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
```

All three carry the same `goal` object, including `goal.baselineProgramCas = sha256:28b5262f…` and the same `createdAt`. Only `id` and `sessionId` differ, and the two extra `sessionId`s are the imported snapshot Sessions. Total runs went from 8 to 10 after the two imports.

**Expected.** A package carries the *result* of a run, not a new run. Either the imported Session references the original run (`sourceRunId`/read-only link), or the copy is marked as a snapshot and excluded from run listings and from `isEvolveRunActive`.

**Why it matters**

- **Run list and counters double.** Anything that lists runs (the task panel, counts, token/cost summaries) shows the same run several times after a few imports.
- **`isEvolveRunActive` can be fooled.** The create dialog's "this Session already has a running experiment" branch is computed from the Session's own runs (`App.tsx:1672`). A copied run that is still `running` at export time would arrive as a second active run for the snapshot Session, blocking creation there for a run the user cannot stop in that Session.
- **Cost and score statistics become wrong** in aggregate views, because the same 223,006 tokens are counted three times.

**Suggested fix.** On import, either drop evolution run records from the package (they are observability data, not research material), or persist them with a `sourceRunId` and treat runs with a `sourceRunId` as snapshots: not active, not counted, and linked to the original.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI at a vite dev server), 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, evolve runtime `127.0.0.1:17676`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright.
- Source Session `5293e460…` (puct run `0098af62`), imported into two snapshot Sessions `fe4d2e3c…` and `b163af95…`.

- The raw `GET /api/evolve/runs` response taken after the imports is attached in the comment below (three entries with identical `tokens`, `candidates`, `bestNodeIndex`, `createdAt`, `goal`).

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A packaged first run re-points `<dataDir>/envs/*/bin/python*` at the bundled interpreter (`fixVenvLaunchers`, `application/src/bootstrap.ts`). The new target is computed as

```ts
const relTarget = posixRelative(venvBinDir, join(paths.python, "bin", "python3"));
```

`posixRelative` is a plain string `posix.relative`. When the data dir and `resourcesPath` reach this function under two spellings of the same physical directory — macOS `/var/folders/...` vs `/private/var/folders/...`, or `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp` — the two paths share no textual prefix, so `relative()` emits a walk to `/` whose `..` count equals the depth of the **creation** spelling. The link then only resolves when its parent is opened through that same spelling. Read through the other spelling (one component deeper, because of `private`), it lands one level short and the target becomes `/private/private/...`, which does not exist.

Observed live during #1374 on a signed `.app` (2026-11-25): with the data dir placed under `$TMPDIR`, `start-stack` fail-fasted with `SHARED_ENV is missing` after the first-run relink wrote links that resolved one directory short. The smoke script now `realpath`s both the data dir and the `.app` path before seeding, so that path no longer reproduces there; the app-side cause is unchanged.

Expected: the relink should resolve for either spelling of the same directory (compute the relative target from real paths, or keep both sides in one spelling before `relative()`).

- macOS 15 (arm64), packaged `ScienceDiscovery.app` built by `application/scripts/build-mac.sh` (ad-hoc signed, `SD_MAC_SIGN=0`), 2026-11-25.
- Data dir under `$TMPDIR` (i.e. `/var/folders/...`), which the app resolves as `/private/var/folders/...`.
- Python/Electron come from the packaged payload; no host toolchain involved.

## Additional Information

- Code: `application/src/bootstrap.ts` — `fixVenvLaunchers` (the `darwin` branch) and `posixRelative`.
- Context: openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery#1374 — the smoke script had to realpath its data dir and `.app` copy to work around this; the PR treats the app-side fault as out of scope.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** When the API service restarts while an evolution run is in flight, the run is marked `failed` and the card in the conversation says only `失败` (failed). There is no reason, no mention that the interruption came from a service restart, and no way to retry from the card.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start a real evolution run from a Session (`puct`, `checkpointMode: auto`, `expansions: 12`).
2. While it is running (I acted after 5 candidates / 11,279 tokens), restart the API: `tmux send-keys -t sd-api C-c`, then `bash ~/sd-test/start-api.sh`.
3. Reload the page, reopen the Session.

**Observed** (`933957a`, run `f548bd3f-c90e-4e0f-8836-e64ddcea2e05`)

- Run created `2026-11-24T17:26:16.761Z`; panel reading at `17:26:42Z`: `tokens=11279`, `candidates=5`.
- API restarted at `17:26:42Z`, back to ready in 22 s.
- Run record after the restart: `status=failed`, `tokens=11279`, `candidates=5`, `finishedAt=2026-11-24T17:27:11.267Z`.
- The card renders `已耗时 54 秒｜自动｜失败` and nothing else.

The good news, which the report should keep: the card does **not** pretend to be running after the restart — the clock stops, the status matches the stored record, and the Token / candidate count / elapsed time do not regress. The gap is only the missing explanation.

**Root cause**

- The persisted run record carries a terminal `status` but no failure reason field (keys: `algorithm, bestNodeIndex, candidates, costCents, createdAt, finishedAt, goal, id, lastSeq, sessionId, startedAt, status, tokens`), so there is nothing to render even if the client wanted to.
- The client card renders the status label and nothing else: `apps/desktop/src/evolve/status.ts:24` `evolveStatusLabel()` returns `TEXT.evolve.status[status]`, and `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveRuns.tsx` prints that pill with the counters.
- Because the reason is never persisted, a restart-induced failure and a genuine search failure (bad evaluator, crashed candidate) look identical.

**Expected.** A failed run should say why — at least distinguish "the service restarted / the connection was lost" from "the search failed" — and should offer a retry that reuses the stored goal (the goal, baseline CAS and scorecard are already persisted).

**Impact**

- The user cannot tell whether the failure is their own goal/evaluator or the environment, so the only safe action is to start over, which costs a full design turn (the design turn for this run consumed 797K tokens) plus the lost candidates.
- A design turn plus a run is the most expensive thing a user does in this client; a silent failure at that price is the worst possible place to stay silent.
- Nothing in the UI suggests that a restart happened; support tickets for this will describe it as "the experiment just failed".

**Suggested fix.** Persist a failure reason (code + message) on the run record when the orchestrator loses its sidecar/connection, render it on the card next to `失败`, and add a retry action that re-creates the run from the persisted `goal`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, evolve sidecar `127.0.0.1:17676`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright; sandbox backend `bwrap`.

Before the restart, the card read `已耗时 54 秒｜自动`; after the reload it reads `自动｜失败`:

![failed evolve run card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/1-failed-run-card.png)

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In the Chinese UI, runtime diagnostics that come from the runner and the sandbox egress path are shown as raw English sentences. The user reads `Shell execution timed out after 5000 ms` or `example.org:443 is not in the sandbox network allowed domains` in the middle of a Chinese conversation.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 超时 › 执行超时` → switch `不限` off, set `5` seconds.
2. Ask the agent to run something slower than 5 s (`python3 -c "import time;time.sleep(10)"`).
3. Reset the timeout, then `设置 › 沙箱网络` → `域名白名单` with only `only.example.org`.
4. Ask the agent to fetch `https://example.org` and press `拒绝` on the network consent card.

**Observed** (`933957a`)

```text
run_shell   → failed — Shell execution timed out after 5000 ms
run_direct_shell → failed — Direct shell execution timed out after 5000 ms
egress deny → Permission denied: Sandbox network ... example.org
              example.org:443 is not in the sandbox network allowed domains
proxy path  → Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden
```

The app already has a localized layer for *run failures* — `apps/desktop/src/run-failure.ts:36` maps `/\b(?:execution|evaluation) timed out after (\d+) ms\b/i` to `TEXT.runFailure.timeoutTitles.runner_exec`, and this run even produced the localized 「调整超时」 card with 「Runner 执行超时（毫秒）」. The English string still reaches the user because it arrives through a **tool result**, which is rendered verbatim, and because the egress/proxy reasons have no mapping at all.

**Root cause**

- `services/runner/src/executor.ts:713` builds the terminal message as `` `${timeoutLabel} timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms` `` — an English sentence produced where no locale is known.
- `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts:273` builds `` `${host}:${port} is not in the sandbox network allowed domains` `` the same way.
- A `Tunnel connection failed: ...` string comes from the HTTP/proxy client and is forwarded untouched.
- The client translates only structured failure codes (`run-failure.ts`); a diagnostic that arrives inside a tool result is displayed as-is, so none of the strings above can be localized by the existing layer.

**Expected.** Either the runner reports a code plus parameters (`runner_exec` + `timeoutMs`) and the client renders `工具执行已超过 5 秒。…` (the string already exists: `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:2342`), or the tool-result surface applies the same translation table the failure card uses. The egress reason should get the same treatment.

**Impact**

- A Chinese user meets an English technical sentence they cannot search for and cannot act on; 「建议缩小单次执行范围后重试，或在系统设置中适当增加执行超时时间」 already exists in `zh.ts` but is never shown.
- The same body of text is also what users paste into bug reports, which makes triage harder than it needs to be.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright; sandbox backend `bwrap`.

### Additional Information

![timeout card and English tool result](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/2-timeout-english.png)

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** `设置 › 沙箱网络 › 域名白名单` reads as a hard boundary, but it is only a starting point: (a) an agent can ask for an extra host and, once the user presses `仅允许一次`, that host is added to the allowlist for the run; and (b) after the user presses `拒绝`, the agent can still reach the same host by switching to the non-sandboxed `run_direct_shell` channel. Neither behaviour is stated on the surfaces where the user makes the decision.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 沙箱网络` → `域名白名单`, fill only `only.example.org`, save.
2. In a Session, ask the agent to fetch `https://example.org` (not on the list).
3. Path (a): press `仅允许一次` on the consent card — the fetch succeeds (HTTP 200, title `Example Domain`).
4. Path (b): press `拒绝` instead — the sandbox refuses, and the agent requests host-level execution, which succeeds.

**Observed** (`933957a`)

- The consent card reads: 「需要权限｜本次 Agent 运行允许 local 上的沙箱网络访问：example.org。用途：用 Python urllib 抓取 https://example.org 的状态码与标题。」 with buttons `仅允许一次 / 允许同类操作 / 拒绝`.
- After approving, `agents-run/sandbox-network-consent.ts` merges the approved hosts into the configured list, so `example.org` is reachable for the rest of the run.
- After denying, the sandbox reports `example.org:443 is not in the sandbox network allowed domains`; the agent then asks for `run_direct_shell` (「直接在主机上执行」), whose card warns only that it does not isolate 「文件系统、进程或网络」, and the same fetch then succeeds from the host.

**Root cause**

- `services/api/src/agent-run/sandbox-network-consent.ts:80` — on `consume()`, the ticket's hosts are appended to the configured domains: `allowedDomains: [...(base.mode === "domain-allowlist" ? base.allowedDomains : []), ...ticket.hosts]`. The design comment says the configured capability is already authorized and only the extra hosts come from the token, so this is intentional; the problem is that the *setting* is named and described as an allowlist, while the effective policy for a run is allowlist + approved hosts.
- `run_direct_shell` runs outside the sandbox, so no egress policy applies to it at all. A refusal in the sandbox therefore does not end the attempt: it changes the channel.

**Expected.** One of:

- keep the widening but say so on both surfaces — the setting's help text ("批准运行中的网络申请会临时把域名加入白名单") and the consent card ("这条授权会覆盖当前的白名单设置");
- or make the direct-execution consent card state explicitly that approving it also bypasses the sandbox network policy, so the user is deciding on the real consequence;
- or, when a network consent was denied earlier in the same run, have the host-execution card mention that the earlier refusal is being routed around.

**Impact**

- A user who configures `域名白名单` to keep the sandbox off the internet will still have the sandbox (and, after one extra approval, the host) reaching hosts outside that list, without a single surface saying so.
- The `拒绝` action reads as a refusal, but it is a refusal *of that channel only* — the agent immediately retries through a wider one, so the safety decision does not hold.
- This is exactly the kind of mismatch that makes a security setting untrustworthy: the control is there, its semantics are not.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411` (`bwrap`); Chromium 1228 via Playwright.

### Additional Information

The consent card shown while the configured allowlist contained only `only.example.org`:

![network consent card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/3-network-consent-card.png)

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `933957a3af51600453da7473646ddd46f0a33cf7` (main, 2026-11-25).
